questions.question: "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so" is stated under ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Fundamental Duties.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• "To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so" is a part of the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
 
• These duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning that they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• -Other duties included in this list are respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood, and striving towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
• 
 
 
 

 Article
 Fundamental duty
 
 

 Article 51A (b) 
 To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
 
 

 Article 51A (c)
 To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India
 
 

 Article 51A (d)
 to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Preamble of the Constitution outlines the basic principles and objectives of the Indian state**, including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• ** The Directive Principles of State Polic**y are **guidelines for the government to follow **in order to establish a just and equitable society.
 
• **The Fundamental Rights **are guaranteed to all citizens and include the** right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, and the right to life and liberty.**

questions.question: On the banks of which river was the war between Harshavardhana and Pulakeshin II fought?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Pulakeshin-II defeated Harshavardhana in the year 618 A.D.

 
 
• ​Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha on the banks of Narmada in the winter of 618-619 CE.
 
• Pulakeshin entered into a treaty with Harsha, with the Narmada River designated as the border between the Chalukya Empire and that of Harshavardhana.
 
 
 
• Emperor Harshavardhana ruled entire North India from Kannauj.
 
 
• He wanted to expand into the South by defeating Pulakeshin-II__.
 
• However, Pulakeshin-II was able to successfully defeat Harshavardhan in the battle on the banks of river Narmada.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Harshavardhana ruled over a major part of north India from 606 to 647 AD.

 
 
• Harshavardhana was the son of Prabhakara Vardhana.​
 
• Xuan Zang also lived in the court of Harshavardhana.
 
• His court poet Banabhatta wrote his biography Harshacharita__. This biography has given rich information about Harshavardhana.
 
• His capital was at Kannauj.
 
• Pulakeshin-II defeated Harshavardhana in the year 618 A.D.
 
 
 
• Pulakeshin II (610–642 CE) was the most famous ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi (present-day Badami in Karnataka, India).
 
 
• During his reign, the Chalukya kingdom expanded to cover most of the Deccan region in peninsular India.
 
 
• Pulakeshin was a son of the Chalukya king Kirttivarman I.
 
 
• When Kirttivarman died, Pulakeshin appears to have been a minor, as Kirttivarman's younger brother Mangalesha became the next king.
 
 
 
• The famous Emperor Pulakeshin II of the Chalukya Dynasty was defeated by Narasimhavarman I of the Pallava Dynasty. Vikramaditya I recaptured Vatapi from Pallavas and restored the Chalukya power.
 
 
• The other titles of Pulakeshin II were Bhattarka and Maharajadhiraja.

questions.question: In shot put, the shot which is a metal ball weighs how many kg for men and women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Men-7.26 kg Women-4 kg.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The shot put is an athletics event where athletes throw a metal ball or shot as far as possible.**
 
• The metal ball or shot used in shot put is made of brass, iron, or steel and has a smooth surface for a better grip.
 
• The weight of the metal ball or shot used in shot put varies for different age groups and gender categories.
 
• Shot put is a part of the track and field events in athletics.
 
• The metal ball or shot used in shot put has a diameter of 110-130 mm for men and 95-110 mm for women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The hammer throw is one of the four throwing events in regular track and field competitions, along with the discus throw, shot put and javelin.
 
• In hammer throws events, athletes throw a metal ball (16lb/7.26kg for men, 4kg/8.8lb for women) that is attached to a grip by a steel wire no longer than 1.22m while remaining inside a seven-foot (2.135m) diameter circle. 
 
• In order for the throw to be measured, the ball must land inside a marked 35-degree sector and the athlete must not leave the circle before it has landed, and then only from the rear half of the circle. 
 
• The thrower usually makes three or four spins before releasing the ball.

questions.question: How many pathways are constructed as independently organized conducting tubes in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** two.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **There two pathways are constructed as independently organized conducting tubes in plants.**
 
• These pathways are** the xylem and phloem, which are responsible for the transport of water, minerals, and nutrients throughout the plant.**
 
• The xylem is responsible for the transport of water and minerals from roots to the leaves, while the phloem is responsible for the transport of nutrients from leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• Understanding the organization and function of xylem and phloem is essential in the study of plant physiology and agriculture.
 
• Both Xylem and Phloem combinedly worked for the conduction in plants.
 
• All plants need water, minerals, and food, Flowering plants have a very well-developed system to transport these substances, this system is called the vascular system.
 
• The vascular system contains two types of tissues, the xylem, and the phloem.
 
• The xylem distributes water and the phloem distributes food throughout the plant's body, this process is known as Conduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• XYLEM:__

 __
 
• It is a plant vascular tissue that conveys water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant and also provides physical support.
 
• Xylem tissue consists of a variety of specialized, water-conducting cells known as tracheary elements.
 
• xylem is found in all vascular plants, including the seedless club mosses, ferns, and horsetails, as well as all angiosperms and gymnosperms.
 
 
 
• PHLOEM:__
 
 
• It is also called bast, tissues in plants that conduct foods made in the leaves to all other parts of the plant.
 
• Phloem is composed of various specialized cells called sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres, and phloem parenchyma cells. 
 
• Two types of Phloem: i) Primary ii) Secondary

questions.question: The ultimate goal of Mission Indradhanush is to ensure full immunization with all available vaccines for children up to ________ years of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** two.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission Indradhanush is a health initiative launched by the Indian government in 2014 with the aim to immunize all children up to the age of two years.**
 
• The program focuses on providing vaccines for** vaccine-preventable diseases such as polio, measles, and hepatitis B, among others**.
 
• It aims to reach out to children in remote and underserved areas and increase the coverage of immunization in the country.
 
• The program has been successful in increasing the immunization coverage in the country from **62% in 2014 to 94% in 2019.**
 
• Immunization is a vital public health intervention that **saves millions of lives every year. It is one of the most cost-effective ways to prevent infectious diseases.**
 
• The World Health Organization recommends that all children receive** routine immunizations to protect them from vaccine-preventable diseases.**
 
• In India, despite the availability of vaccines, **many children still miss out on immunization due to various reasons such as lack of awareness, accessibility, and affordability.**
 
• Mission Indradhanush aims to address these gaps and ensure that every child in the country is protected from vaccine-preventable diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• To further intensify the immunization programme, launched the Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) on October 8, 2017. 
 
• The aim of Mission Indradhanush and Intensified Mission Indradhanush is to boost the routine immunization coverage 
 
• Again, the Government of India has introduced Intensified Mission Indradhanush 2.0 to ensure reaching the unreached with all available vaccines and accelerate the coverage of children and pregnant women in the identified districts and blocks from 2019-2020.

questions.question: In India, in relation to Census, what is the full form of NPR?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Population Register.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **NPR stands for National Population Register.**
 
• It is a **database** maintained by the Government of India containing demographic and biometric details of **every citizen of the country.**
 
• The data collected through** NPR is used for various government schemes **and programs such as the issuance of Aadhaar cards, voter ID cards, and passports.
 
• NPR is updated periodically to ensure the accuracy of data and to include new citizens who have turned **18 years of age.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The NPR is a record of all the **usual residents of the country**.
 
• It is mandatory for every usual resident of India to register in the NPR.
 
• The NPR includes both Indian citizens and foreign citizens.
 
• The primary objective of the NPR is to create a comprehensive database of every usual resident in the country.
 
• **The NPR is prepared at various levels, including local (village/sub-town), sub-district, district, state, and national levels. This is done under the provisions of the Citizenship Act 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003.**
 
• The data for the National Population Register was first collected in 2010 by the Government of India. The exercise is repeated every 10 years.
 
• The aim is to create a comprehensive identity database of every usual resident in the country. The database would contain both demographic and biometric details.
 
• The government ha**s clarified that no documents will be required for NPR **as a self-declaration will suffice for data entry in the population register.

questions.question: Which sector runs nearly 60 percent of dispensaries in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Private Sector.**__

__
 
• **The private sector runs nearly 60 percent of dispensaries in India.**
 
• Private dispensaries are owned and operated by** private individuals or organizations.**
 
• The cooperative sector refers to dispensaries run by cooperatives, which are** owned and operated by a group of individuals for their mutual benefit.**
 
• The joint sector refers to dispensaries run jointly by the** government and private individuals or organizations.**
 
• The public sector refers to** dispensaries run by the government.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The private sector has been playing a significant role in providing healthcare services in India, especially in urban areas.
 
• The cooperative sector has a limited presence in the healthcare sector in India.
 
• The joint sector has been encouraged by the government to improve healthcare infrastructure in the country.
 
• The public sector has the largest number of dispensaries in India but often faces challenges in providing quality healthcare services due to lack of resources and infrastructure.

questions.question: Microfinance is a ________ service.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** financial.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Microfinance is a way in which loans, credit, insurance, access to savings accounts, and money transfers are provided to small business owners and entrepreneurs in underdeveloped parts of India.
 
• Microfinance is a form of financial service that provides small loans and other financial services to poor and low-income households, hence it is an economic tool designed to promote financial inclusion which enables the poor and low-income households to come out of poverty, increase their income levels, and improve overall living standards.
 
• The beneficiaries of microfinance are those who do not have access to traditional financial resources.
 
• Interest rates on microloans are generally higher than those on a traditional personal loan as the amount of the loan is small. 
 
• Features of microfinance:
 
 
• The borrowers are generally from low-income backgrounds. 
 
• Loans availed under microfinance are usually of small amounts, i.e., microloans. 
 
• The loan tenure is short.
 
• Microfinance loans do not require any collateral. *Hence statement 3 is not correct.*
 
• These loans are usually repaid at higher frequencies.
 
• The purpose of most microfinance loans is income generation.
 
• The end result of microloans should be to have its recipients outgrow smaller loans and be ready for traditional bank loans.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Production **refers to the process of creating goods or services, and it is not related to microfinance.
 
• ** Software production** is a specific type of production that involves creating software applications, and it is also not related to microfinance.
 
• ** Waste management **refers to the collection, transportation, and disposal of waste materials, and it is not related to microfinance.

questions.question: In India, the Green Revolution increased the production of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wheat crops witnessed the maximum rate of increase in production due to the Green Revolution in India.
 
• The Green Revolution started in 1965 with the first introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds in Indian agriculture.
 
• This was coupled with better and more efficient irrigation and the correct use of fertilizers to boost the crop.
 
 
• The result of the Green Revolution was to make India self-sufficient when it came to food grains.
 
 
 
• These HYV seeds had more success with the wheat crop and were highly effective in regions that had proper irrigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Green Revolution, spreading over the period from 1967-68 to 1977-78, changed India’s status from a food-deficient country to one of the world's leading agricultural nations.
 
• The Green Revolution resulted in a great increase in the production of food grains (especially wheat and rice) due to the introduction of developing countries of new, high-yielding variety seeds, beginning in the mid-20th century.
 
• The Green Revolution was an endeavor initiated by Norman Borlaug in the 1960s.
 
• He is known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in the world.
 
• It led to him winning the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his work in developing High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat.
 
• In India, the Green Revolution was mainly led by M.S. Swaminathan.
 
• Revolution- Related to
 
 
• Blue - Fish Production
 
• Silver Fibre - Cotton Production
 
• Green - Agriculture Production
 
• Black - Petroleum Production
 
• Grey - Fertilizer Production
 
• Pink - Onions, Prawn Production
 
• Red - Meat, Tomato Production
 
• Silver - Egg Production

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Which among the following elements behaves like alkali metals as well as halogens in its properties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Hydrogen.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen behaves like alkali metals as it has one electron in its outermost shell, which it readily loses to form a cation.**
 
• Hydrogen also behaves like halogens as it can share its electrons with other elements to form a covalent bond.
 
• This property of hydrogen is due to its position in the periodic table, where it is placed above the alkali metals and halogens.
 
• Helium and neon are noble gases and do not exhibit properties of either alkali metals or halogens.
 
• Lithium behaves like an alkali metal, but not like a halogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Neon is a noble gas **and does not readily react with other elements to form compounds.
 
• ** Helium is the second lightest element** and is used in balloons, airships, and cooling systems.
 
• **Lithium is a soft, silvery-white metal** that is highly reactive and is used in batteries, ceramics, and pharmaceuticals.

questions.question: In which year the Asian Games were held for the second time in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1982.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The Games were regulated by the Asian Games Federation from the first Games in New Delhi, India, until the 1978 Games.
 
• It was firstly organized in the 1951 Asian Games in New Delhi, India.
 
• New Delhi, the national capital of India, has hosted the Asian Games on two occasions: the inaugural 1951 Asian Games and the 1982 Asian Games.
 
• Asian Games, 2023 will be a multi-sport event celebrated in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• There have been nine nations that have hosted the Asian Games. Forty-six nations have participated in the Games, including Israel, which was excluded from the Games altogether after Israel managed to win a silver medal (in their last participation) at the 1974 Asian Games in Iran. The most recent games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia from 18 August to 2 September 2018.
 
• The Asian Games Movement uses symbols to represent the ideals embodied in the Asian Games charter.

questions.question: What is used to measure the magnitude of an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Richter Scale.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Richter scale:

 
• Richter scale is used for measuring the intensity of earthquakes.
 
• The Richter scale measures the maximum amplitude of seismic waves as they reach seismographs.
 
• The magnitude is expressed in absolute numbers, 0-10.
 
• The power of an earthquake is expressed in terms of magnitude on a scale called the Richter scale.
 
• This was developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935.
 
• The intensity scale is named after Mercalli, an Italian seismologist.
 
• The intensity scale takes into account the visible damage caused by the event.
 
• The range of intensity scale is from 1-12.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f471c13d4cc94dd5c22647b44ea83fc35469cccaeb8d6a0a7020e63b51ad2723.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e744b6360c30fd0c2e8cd8d2283ac52aaf4cbb8673ec643232e7ed21d9afd34.png] 

 
• There are three types of earthquake waves:

 
 
• P waves or longitudinal waves
 
• S waves or transverse waves
 
• L waves or surface waves
 
 

Hence, the Richter scale is used to measure Seismic vibrations.

questions.question: Who won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in Manipuri in 2018?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akham Lakshmi Devi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shrimati Akham Lakshmi Devi was born on May 1, 1952, in Imphal, Manipur.
 
• She received her training in Manipuri dance from Gurus Amubi Singh, Tomba Singh, and Th. Babu Singh.
 
• She specialized in Manipuri dance at the Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy in Imphal.
 
• Shrimati Akham Lakshmi Devi has performed in various prestigious dance festivals, including the Bhagyachandra national dance festival and those organized by the Manipur State Kala Akademi and Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• Her performances in dance productions by the Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy, such as Keibul Lamjao, Ramayan, Lei Langba, Moirang Sha, and Geet Govinda, have received critical acclaim.
 
• She has received several honors, including the Manipur State Kala Akademi Award in 2010 and the Nritya Bhusan in 2014.
 
• Shrimati Akham Lakshmi Devi was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for her significant contributions to Manipuri dance.
